title: A More Equitable Certificate of Entitlement
what_it_is: A More Equitable Certificate of Entitlement

sections.label: PSP hybrid COE system proposal
sections.summary: PSP proposes a hybrid COE system using economic and social factors for Categories A, B and D private vehicles.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: However, for private vehicles, PSP believes that even though not everyone in Singapore will be able to own a car, we should also consider the needs of certain groups in society in deciding who gets to own a car.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We would, therefore, like to propose a hybrid COE system that takes into account both economic and social factors in the allocation of private vehicles, which will only apply to Categories A, B and D COEs.

sections.label: COE credits for citizens and PRs
sections.summary: PSP proposes bidding for Categories A, B and D COEs with Government-distributed COE credits, allocated by factors like nationality, children, age and disability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Therefore, today I would like to propose a feasible COE system that takes into account needs factors for the Government's consideration.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We propose that instead of bidding for Categories A, B and D COEs using cash, bids should be placed using COE credits.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: COE credits will be distributed by Government to adult Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents (PRs) each month.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The number of COE credits received by each person will depend on various factors, such as nationality, the number of children, age, disability and so forth.

sections.label: COE Government revenue share
sections.summary: COE accounted for an estimated $4.66 billion in FY2023, about 4.5% of total Government revenue.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: COE is a significant revenue source for the Government, accounting for an estimated $4.66 billion in revenue in FY2023, or about 4.5% of total Government revenue.

sections.label: Flat fee COE option
sections.summary: The first option is a flat fee of $50,000 per Category A COE and $70,000 per Category B COE.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: First option, a flat fee of say $50,000 per Category A (Cat A) COE and $70,000 per Cat B COE.

sections.label: COE credits for citizens and PRs
sections.summary: PSP proposes a COE credit bidding system for private cars and motorcycles, giving 100 credits to adult citizens and 70 to adult PRs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: PSP proposes that instead of bidding for Categories A, B, and D using cash, for private cars and motorcycles, we create a new bidding system using "COE credits" .

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For example, we could give 100 credits to each adult Singaporean citizen and 70 credits to each adult permanent resident.

sections.label: COE base fee proposal
sections.summary: PSP proposes car owners pay a COE base fee in addition to bidding with credits, since abandoning COE income would create a fiscal gap.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The income from COEs is a considerable sum, and abandoning it entirely would create a large fiscal gap.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Therefore, we propose that in addition to bidding with credits, car owners must pay a COE base fee.

sections.label: Category A and B COE base fees
sections.summary: Suggests base COE fees of $50,000 for Category A and $70,000 for Category B.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For example, the base fee for a Category A COE could be set at $50,000, and Category B at $70,000.

sections.label: ARF increase and multiple-car fee
sections.summary: Suggests implementing the option by raising the Additional Registration Fee and charging households with more than one car.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: If this option is chosen, it could be implemented by increasing the Additional Registration Fee (ARF).

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We also suggest that households purchasing more than one car should pay an additional fee.

sections.label: Fairness and alternative COE policy
sections.summary: States the alternative policies may not be most economically efficient but can treat citizens more fairly, and calls on government to consider them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: While these alternative policies may not be the most economically efficient when viewed purely from an economic perspective, we believe our alternative policies can treat all citizens more fairly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We call on the government to seriously consider the alternative COE policy we have proposed today. : Mr Speaker, fairness should be at the heart of our public policies as our nation progresses economically.

sections.label: Cut-and-fill COE supply increase
sections.summary: States government increased supply via cut-and-fill for Cats A, B and D, raising 2024 Cats A and B quota by over 9,000.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: The Government cannot control demand, but we have made significant moves to increase supply, including through the "cut-and-fill" approach for Cats A, B and D where we bring forward COEs from the peak supply years to fill the current trough.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: In 2024, we increased the Cats A and B quota by more than 9,000 via "cut-and-fill".

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: The quota released was more than 30% higher than what it would have been without "cut-and-fill".

sections.label: PQP fall and COE injection
sections.summary: States PQP across Cats A, B, C and D fell 5% to 20%, with up to 20,000 more COEs injected, while maintaining the car-lite vision.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Since then, the Prevailing Quota Premium, or PQP, across Cats A, B, C and D have come down by between 5% and 20%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: The additional injection of up to 20,000 COEs is made possible due to changes in travel patterns after COVID-19 and enhanced capabilities to manage traffic congestion with ERP 2.0.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: This increase in supply is the most direct way to give more households the choice of owning a car, without causing traffic congestion.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: More importantly, we remain committed to our shared car-lite vision where walk, cycle, ride are the predominant travel modes.

sections.label: Bus Connectivity Enhancement Programme
sections.summary: States the Bus Connectivity Enhancement Programme was launched last year to enhance the bus network.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Last year, we have also launched the Bus Connectivity Enhancement Programme to enhance the bus network.

sections.label: Sitting tomorrow starts 11am

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Pursuant to Standing Order 2(3)(a), I wish to inform hon Members that the Sitting tomorrow will commence at 11.00 am.
